title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization with Failure Trajectories
claim: Weak-model successful and failed trajectories are merged into a tree that supervises a stronger model.
layout: 2 dashed panels, left-to-right; trajectories feed a tree, then a strong agent
description: The figure has two dashed panels. The left panel stacks two rounded boxes, a blue Successful Trajectory and a red Failure Trajectory. Each box holds a task prompt ("Measure the temperature of sodium chloride"), a Weak Agent robot icon, and a short chain of action boxes such as Look around and Focus on the thermometer, with ellipses between them. The failure box ends in a wrong action, "Focus on the solium". The right panel, labeled Trajectory Tree, shows the merged trajectories as a tree. It starts at the prompt and branches into oval action nodes. Blue ovals mark successful actions and red ovals mark failed ones. Stars, yellow circles, check and cross marks, and happy and sad faces annotate the nodes. Red and black arrows show the paths. A large triangle arrow at the far right points to a Strong Agent head icon. The eye goes first to the colorful tree.
caption: Illustration of the trajectory tree construction and the weak-to-strong generalization with trajectories. The left part explores different trajectories with a weak model. A trajectory tree is constructed by merging the same action path. Nodes on the tree represent different actions and performing different actions will lead to various subsequent paths. Then the trajectory tree is used to elicit the ability of the strong model.
abstract: Weak-to-Strong generalization (W2SG) is a new trend to elicit the full capabilities of a strong model with supervision from a weak model. While existing W2SG studies focus on simple tasks like binary classification, we extend this paradigm to complex interactive decision-making environments. Specifically, we fine-tune a strong model with trajectories of intermediate actions generated by a weak model. Motivated by the human learning process, we propose to generalize not only successful knowledge but also failed experiences so that the strong model can learn from the failed trajectories accumulated by weak models. To effectively and efficiently elicit the potential of strong agents, we further construct ``trajectory trees," a hierarchical representation that organizes weak model-generated action trajectories, coupled with Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to optimize the strong model. Through theoretical analysis, we provide formal guarantees for the effectiveness of our method in improving W2SG performance. Our empirical evaluations demonstrate substantial improvements in reasoning and decision-making capabilities across diverse task domains, validating the scalability and robustness of our proposed framework. Our code is available at: https://github.com/yeruimeng/TraTree.git.
